name: Razor code-behind splitter
tagline: Move inline @code blocks out of .razor markup into .razor.cs partial classes.
description: Every component in the repo is a markup file plus a code-behind. This lifts each `@code { ... }` body into `<Component>.razor.cs`, picking the namespace the Razor compiler generates for the markup half so the two partials meet. Members that render markup (`RenderFragment X => __builder => { <div/> }`) are Razor syntax rather than C#, so those stay behind in a trimmed `@code` block. Code-behinds do not inherit `_Imports.razor`, so generated files start with a thin using list and the build says what else they need.

commands.blurb: List components still holding an inline @code block; exits non-zero when any remain
Split every component under a path (defaults to the whole repo)
Top a code-behind up with the _Imports.razor usings its markup half had, after a build reports a missing type
Drop usings for repo namespaces a code-behind never references

notes: Run split, build the solution, then --add-imports on the files that failed and --prune to trim the result; repeat until the build is clean
A using alias only comes across when the moved code names it, because aliases resolve from the global namespace in a .cs file but from the enclosing namespace in markup
An alias cannot rescue a name an enclosing namespace also declares (Lyo.DataTable vs a DataTable type); qualify those references instead
--prune only judges namespaces declared in this repo, since it cannot see the types inside a NuGet package
